text:
ian: quick idea — we should add an explicit checkpoint compatibility negotiation step between the loader and the scheduler. avoids silent conversions and gives the runtime a signal about fallback cost.
rachel: sketch the handshake?
ian: loader responds to a lightweight meta request. something like:
```http
GET /checkpoint/meta?path=/models/foomodel
200 {format: "safetensors", version: "1.2", sharding: "sharded", shards: 8, checksum: "sha256:abcd...", compat_tier: 2, can_zero_copy: true}
```
ian: compat_tier is our judgment on how many runtime features the checkpoint needs. 0 = plain tensors, 1 = needs name-mapping, 2 = requires index-merge hints, 3 = needs conversion/rehydration.
mike: I like the explicit tiers. how do we compute compat_tier? heuristics in the indexer during ingest?
sophia: yes — indexer sets the tier. we can also allow a runtime override when we detect missing features at load-time (fallthrough to on-demand conversion).
rachel: can we return an estimated conversion cost in the meta response? so scheduler can decide whether to route to a node with conversion capacity or to a fallback model variant.
ian: good call. add `conversion_cost_ms` and `conversion_mem_mb`. example: `{conversion_cost_ms: 4200, conversion_mem_mb: 32000}`
sophia: edge case: model zip that contains a mix of pt & safetensors blobs. how does the handshake express mixed-format shards?
mike: propose allowing per-shard descriptors in the meta response. e.g. `shard_map: [{id:0, format:safetensors, size_mb:120}, {id:1, format:pt, size_mb:118}, ...]`
ian: Yea. that lets scheduler prefer nodes with the right cached shard formats. also helps us implement partial on-the-fly conversion for only PT shards.
sophia: security note — we must include `signed_manifest` or `manifest_sig` so private deployments can enforce authenticity before conversion.
rachel: +1. include `manifest_sig` and `signer_key_id`.
loadbot: deploybot: meta-request logged for /models/foomodel by ian@eng at 4299123456
mike: operationally, we should not block warmup path on conversion. warmup should be probabilistic: if compat_tier <=1, eager warmup; if >=2, warmup only index and map; conversion flagged to run async with low pri.
ian: agreed. add new field in meta `warmup_recommendation: eager|index-only|defer-conversion`.
sophia: API and on-disk format: we should keep this negotiation format backward compatible. if a loader doesn't support meta, it returns 204 and the scheduler falls back to legacy probing (try load -> fail -> convert).
rachel: decision proposal: implement the meta handshake in indexer v2, add compat_tier & per-shard descriptors, and scheduler uses `conversion_cost_ms` + `warmup_recommendation` to choose route. legacy loaders get 204 and trigger existing fallback.
mike: perf experiment to run: sample 500 model loads, compare end-to-end latency with and without preflight negotiation when mixed-format shards exist. put numbers in the `#benchmarks` channel.
sophia: I'll add the manifests schema PR and a converter prototype. planning to land indexer v2 fields next sprint.
ian: thanks — this should reduce surprise conversions and make routing/capacity decisions explicit. :thumbsup:
rachel: SGTM.
